summary.headline: SAMHI Q1 FY27: same-store RevPAR up 9.6% to Rs 5,220 at 79.3% occupancy, while reported EBITDA fell 4% YoY on a one-time base and GST impact.
summary.overview: Total income rose 7.3% YoY to Rs 308.3 crore reported, or 10.8% on a comparable basis after excluding Rs 9.3 crore one-time other income in the prior-year base. Same-store revenue grew about 9.1% and same-store RevPAR grew 9.6%, with occupancy up to 79.3% from 74.2%. Reported EBITDA fell about 4% YoY, which management attributes to a one-time Rs 9.2 crore GST impact and a prior-year one-time item; comparable EBITDA margin was about 12.1%. Management also sought a board enabling resolution for a Rs 750 crore capital raise, which drew heavy analyst questioning.

financial_highlights.change: +7.3% YoY reported; +10.8% comparable (ex Rs 9.3 crore one-time income in base)

financial_highlights.value: about Rs 100 crore (per analyst's math, not stated as a figure by management)
financial_highlights.change: down about 4% YoY reported; comparable margin about 12.1%

financial_highlights.value: about 3.2x TTM; about 2.4x for operating assets excluding growth capital

financial_highlights.change: about 300 bps lower than at IPO
unchanged since last upgrade in FY26

segments.name: Upper upscale portfolio
segments.commentary: Occupancy 78.4% in Q1 with RevPAR growth below mid-scale; management says the raw ARR growth was about 3.5%-4% across all segments.

segments.name: Mid-scale portfolio
segments.commentary: RevPAR grew 13.7% with occupancy at 81.3%, outperforming the broader upscale portfolio in the quarter.

segments.name: RARE India (asset-light leisure)
segments.commentary: 75 hotels, 1,046 rooms across 15 states; management guides Rs 100-120 crore top line and Rs 35-40 crore EBITDA once stabilised in about 1.5-2 years, against about Rs 47 crore invested to date.

segments.name: F&B
segments.commentary: F&B revenue grew about 3.7-4% YoY against room revenue growth of about 14%, attributed to a shift to domestic guests, a Bangalore restaurant renovation and event cancellations moved into July-August.

guidance_outlook: Long-term same-store revenue growth expectation of 9%-11% reiterated; management says the same-store total revenue growth of about 9%-9.5% sits within this range.

Business plan targets revenue from about Rs 1,200 crore to about Rs 3,000 crore and cumulative free cash flow of over Rs 3,000 crore over FY27-FY31 (the call says Rs 2,000 crore once in error, corrected to Rs 3,000 crore).
Upscale share of revenue expected to rise from about 40%-41% today to about 60% by FY30.
Net debt/EBITDA of about 2.4x expected by FY28, not by end FY27 as an analyst assumed.
GST margin drag to be lower in H2 than H1; YoY GST impact of about Rs 9 crore to be removed from Q3 onward.
Early July trends described as ahead of Q1 exit, with growth split about evenly between rate and occupancy; management cautioned that one month is not representative.
capex_capacity: Seven new hotels in the committed pipeline total 1,660 rooms, mostly upper upscale and upscale; about 450 rooms are being rebranded from upper midscale to upscale.
W Hyderabad targeted for full operation in 2H FY28 (or calendar 2027); management flagged possible regulatory delays.
Courtyard Pune: back-office and MEP renovation under way; public area and guest room renovation deferred to about April 2027, taking 5-6 months.
Navi Mumbai (100% SAMHI-owned, outside the GIC JV): on-site start targeted for 1 April 2027, with a 3-4 year build; capex to stay small through FY28 and ramp in FY29-FY30.

Uttarakhand (Binsar, Almora) 8-acre estate Itmenaan acquisition for about Rs 12 crore; total leisure capital including RARE around Rs 60 crore, with management expecting leisure to stay near 10% of capital allocation.
demand_pricing: Office absorption in core markets about 11 million sq ft in Q1, against about 58 million sq ft for FY26; Bangalore, Hyderabad and Pune were over 65% of GCC leasing.
Passenger traffic was roughly flat YoY in Q1 after an early-quarter dip tied to geopolitics and Gulf carrier limits; the latter half recovered.
Domestic guests rose to 82% of room nights sold from 78% a year ago; 36% of days had occupancy above 90%.
Rate growth was soft because international guests, who pay a 10-20% premium, declined; management expects rate to recover in H2 as the mix rebalances.
Upscale and upper upscale hotels earn about 4x the revenue per key of midscale hotels on a same-store basis in FY26.
GST change from 12% with input tax credit to 5% without it cost about Rs 9.2 crore in Q1 and hits midscale rooms priced below Rs 7,500 more than upscale.

qa_highlights.question: Karan Khanna (Ambit): Why acquire the Itmenaan estate given weak revenue history, how is Leisure capital allocation growing, and what RARE opportunities are being evaluated?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the hotel was idle for about a year and a half after owners moved to Canada and was delisted from RARE; it expects relisting and repricing toward Rs 20,000-40,000 rates in Kumaon. Total RARE capital is about Rs 47 crore, about Rs 60 crore with Itmenaan, and leisure should stay near 10% of capital allocation.

qa_highlights.question: Karan Khanna: How much of FY27 growth is rate versus occupancy, and has July shown a sharp recovery?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said occupancy drives growth in the first six months, with rate recovering in H2 as domestic mix rebalances from 82% toward a higher-premium international mix. July is 'trending far ahead' of Q1 exit, with rate growth now visible, but management declined to give numbers and cautioned one month is not representative.

qa_highlights.question: Jinesh Joshi (PL Capital): Are RARE sign-ups to the Marriott Outdoor Collection program on track, and why must the Rs 750 crore enabling resolution be taken now?
qa_highlights.answer: About 40 of 75 RARE hotels have agreed to join; management said sign-ups are ahead of its expectations and the pace is the issue, with 10-12 hotels on rival platforms. On the resolution, management said it will be taken every year so the Board can act in time; no specific deal is identified.

qa_highlights.question: Vikas Ahuja (Antique): Is the ADR slowdown (about 2.6-2.7% growth) due to West Asia disruption and Marriott-led inventory, and is occupancy at about 79% a tactical rate trade-off?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said rate is soft because inbound international travel fell, and it focuses on same-store total revenue growth of about 9%-9.5%, within the 9%-11% long-term range. In July, total revenue growth split about half rate and half occupancy.

qa_highlights.question: Vikas Ahuja: Why an equity-linked enabling resolution rather than debt, given the investment surplus discussed at the Analyst Day?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the resolution is a general enabling step to respond to unknown problems or opportunities and keep the balance sheet strong. It added that the Rs 1,200 crore to Rs 3,000 crore revenue path has no assumed acquisitions.

qa_highlights.question: Shrinjana Mittal (MS Capital): Is upper upscale underperforming midscale because of downtrading, and why is GST drag above 2%?
qa_highlights.answer: Raw ARR growth was about 3.5%-4% across segments, and midscale RevPAR grew 13.7% at 81.3% occupancy versus 78.4% for upper upscale. GST drag is larger in Q1 and Q2 from volume sales below Rs 7,500, is lower in H2, and is about 2% per management.

qa_highlights.question: Vaibhav Muley (Haitong): Why did F&B growth slow to about 4%, and what is the GIC partnership scope?
qa_highlights.answer: F&B grew about 3.5%-4% against room revenue growth of 14%, due to a shift to domestic guests (80%-83%), a Bangalore restaurant renovation, and West Asia-related event cancellations moved to July-August. GIC has a right to 35% of new upscale deals post-JV, with no talks on existing assets; Navi Mumbai and W Hyderabad are 100% SAMHI-owned.

qa_highlights.question: Prashant Biyani (Elara): Timing for Grand Hyatt pre-positioning at Hyatt Regency Pune, W Hyderabad and Courtyard Pune openings?
qa_highlights.answer: Grand Hyatt repositioning is not being pursued. W Hyderabad is targeted for full operation in 2H FY28 or calendar 2027, with regulatory delays possible. Courtyard Pune public areas and guest room renovation is deferred to about April 2027 for 5-6 months.

qa_highlights.question: Karan Gupta (Asit C Mehta): How does RARE revenue recognition work, and what are RARE's revenue, margin and EBITDA targets?
qa_highlights.answer: RARE earns booking commission and, in some hotels, higher revenue share akin to franchise fees; hotel room revenue stays with owners. Management guides Rs 100-120 crore top line at about 35% margin and Rs 35-40 crore EBITDA once stabilised in about 1.5-2 years.

qa_highlights.question: Viraj Mahadevia (Moneygrow): Can RARE ROCE double the group's roughly 10%, and why is EBITDA flat while PBT is up 25%?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said RARE could reach 5x group ROCE and target 50%-55% ROCE, with about 95% EBITDA-to-PBT flow-through and no finance cost. On EBITDA, it cited the Rs 9 crore one-time other income in the prior-year base and about Rs 9 crore GST drag, with YoY relief from Q3.

qa_highlights.question: Bharat Gianani (MC Research): Does the annual enabling resolution overhang equity, and how is ROCE on acquisitions in a costlier market?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said such provisions are common among capital-intensive peers and no debt-equity mix has been decided. It said acquisitions still target operationally distressed assets, even at market peaks, with renovation, rebranding and asset management as the value levers.

qa_highlights.question: Ashish (Leo Capital): What is the Navi Mumbai status, timeline and capex phasing?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said legacy issues are resolved, with statutory approvals expected in the next few months and design work to be presented next quarter. On-site start is targeted for 1 April 2027, with a 3-4 year build, capex small through FY28, and main spend in FY29-FY30.

risks_watch: Rate softness from lower international inbound mix: rate growth is expected to recover only in H2 FY27, and July's split is one month of data.

EBITDA trajectory: Q1 reported EBITDA was down about 4% YoY; the one-time Rs 9 crore base item and about Rs 9.2 crore GST drag should fall out from Q2 and Q3, but management has not guided EBITDA figures.
Leverage path: management says about 2.4x net debt/EBITDA is reached by FY28, not end-FY27, and disputes an analyst's assumption of 2.5x by year-end.
Equity dilution overhang from the Rs 750 crore enabling resolution, which management says will be taken annually; no use or debt-equity mix defined.
Project execution: W Hyderabad could slip past 2H FY28 due to regulatory approvals; Courtyard Pune renovation timeline depends on April 2027 start; Navi Mumbai on-site start in April 2027.
RARE execution: Marriott Outdoor Collection sign-ups (about 40 of 75 hotels) and RARE's shift to fee income with limited disclosure of RARE RevPAR.
key_quotes: Same-store RevPAR grew 9.6% year-on-year to approximately Rs. 5,220, with portfolio occupancy at 79.3%, which was up from 74.2% in the year-ago quarter.
Put simply, every new upscale key we now add brings in more revenue per key and a better margin than the midscale it often replaces or sits alongside.
We didn't say 2.5x by end of FY 2027. We think we will get there by FY 2028, both because of EBITDA.
Navi Mumbai, we were originally planning to be on-site, hit the ground by end of this fiscal year.
summary.management_tone: Confident on operating metrics, occupancy and the 9%-11% long-term revenue growth band, but defensive and repetitive on the Rs 750 crore enabling resolution, which it frames as routine governance. It was cautious on rate recovery and on July trends, declining to give numbers and warning that one month is not representative.
